results.reader_what: This study explores how small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in the European Earth Observation (EO) sector leverage Artificial Intelligence (AI)
results.reader_more: This study explores how small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in the European Earth Observation (EO) sector leverage Artificial Intelligence (AI) to develop innovative business models. Amid the rapid diffusion of AI technologies and increasing availability of open satellite data, SMEs are emerging as key players in the evolving EO landscape. Drawing on a multiple case study of ten AI-enabled SMEs across the EO value chain, the research identifies two distinct business model archetypes: Specialized AI Services for Space Missions and Data & Knowledge as a Service.

results.reader_more: Despite growing concerns over energy security, infrastructure planning and modelling for emerging green fuel supply chains often neglect risks from supply disruptions. Using a stochastic optimisation model of EU hydrogen imports, we show that 'naive' infrastructure planning results in welfare losses of 12 % (24 billion EUR) compared to risk-aware planning that anticipates supply disruptions. results.reader_more: This study examines how energy resilience was discursively constructed in EU media debates during the energy crisis triggered by Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022 and explores the implications of these constructions for Europe's sustainable energy transition. Existing research has primarily focused on energy security concerns, policy shifts and changing transition priorities following the Russo-Ukrainian war. results.reader_what: Scholars have long feared that regional economic specialization, fostered by freer trade, would make the European Union vulnerable to economic
results.reader_more: Scholars have long feared that regional economic specialization, fostered by freer trade, would make the European Union vulnerable to economic downturn. The most acute concerns have been over the adoption of the common currency: by adopting the euro, countries renounce their ability to meet an asymmetric shock with independent revaluations of their currencies. We systematically test the prediction that regional specialization increases vulnerability to economic downturn using a novel dataset that covers all of the EU’s subnational regions and major sectors of the economy between 2000 and 2013.
